geo_ui_render_intent_tool.name: geo_ui_render_intent_tool
geo_ui_render_intent_tool.description:
Render a GeoIntent as a NASA Worldview permalink URL.

Use this tool to materialise the agent's intended application state
(expressed as a GeoIntent) into a URL the user can open. The agent
reasons in GeoIntent terms, not Worldview-specific URL params.

INPUT FIELD DESCRIPTIONS:
- **intent**: GeoIntent describing the desired application state. Core fields: viewport (bbox + crs), time (instant), layers (id + visible + opacity). Extensions are pre-declared by this tool: do not write `geoui_extensions`; just add the namespaced fields of the extensions the request needs. Supported: compare → compare:layers, compare:active_side, compare:time, compare:mode, compare:value; chart → chart:layer, chart:area, chart:time, chart:autoload; raster-styling → on each LayerRef: raster-styling:palettes, raster-styling:style, raster-styling:min, raster-styling:max, raster-styling:squash. Call geo_ui_list_intent_extensions_tool for their field types.
- **embed_mode**: If True, opens Worldview in embed mode (em=true): minimal chrome intended for iframes, with most UI controls hidden. Default False opens the full interactive Worldview app.

OUTPUT FIELD DESCRIPTIONS:
- **url**: Worldview permalink URL that opens the map at the requested state.

intent.description:
The GeoUI Protocol root.

Carries the minimal cross-application contract: viewport, time,
layers. Extension fields are namespaced (e.g. `"compare:layers"`)
and live as extra keys; their semantics are defined by the schemas
pointed to by `geoui_extensions`.

viewport.description:
Spatial viewport.

`bbox` is interpreted in `crs`. For the geographic default
(`EPSG:4326`), `bbox` is `[west, south, east, north]` in degrees.
For projected CRSs, the values are projected coordinates.
`bbox=None` means "app default extent."

anyOf.description:
Time selection.

Either a single `instant` OR a closed range `{start, end}` — the two
are mutually exclusive. All fields `None` is allowed and means
"app default time."

items.description:
A reference to a renderable layer.

`id` is application-defined — the conforming app must be able to
resolve it to a layer in its own catalogue. Per-layer rendering hints
beyond the universal set (`visible`, `opacity`) belong in extensions
and are expressed as namespaced extra keys
(e.g. `"raster-styling:palettes": [...]`).

url.description: Worldview permalink URL that opens the map at the requested state.

geo_ui_get_state_tool.name: geo_ui_get_state_tool
geo_ui_get_state_tool.description:
Read the current Worldview application state as a GeoIntent.

Use this to observe the state implied by a Worldview URL — typically
when continuing an iterative analysis: read current state, decide
what to change, emit a new GeoIntent via ``geoui_render_intent``.

Auto-injected base reflectance and reference overlay layers are
preserved in the output for fidelity; ignore them when computing
refinements.

INPUT FIELD DESCRIPTIONS:
- **url**: Worldview permalink URL to parse.

OUTPUT FIELD DESCRIPTIONS:
- **intent**: GeoIntent describing the application state encoded in the URL.

geo_ui_list_intent_extensions_tool.name: geo_ui_list_intent_extensions_tool
geo_ui_list_intent_extensions_tool.description:
List the intent extensions this Worldview deployment supports.

Each entry names an extension (compare, chart, raster-styling, ...), says
where its fields live (`scope`: "intent" = namespaced keys on the GeoIntent
root, "layer" = namespaced keys on each LayerRef), gives a one-line
summary of when to use it, its namespaced `keys`, which of them are
`required`, and the JSON schema of its fields.

Decide which extensions the user's request needs, then fill only their
namespaced fields in the GeoIntent you pass to geo_ui_render_intent_tool.
Supported extensions are pre-declared by that tool, so never write
`geoui_extensions` yourself; fields of an unsupported extension are
rejected.

OUTPUT FIELD DESCRIPTIONS:
- **extensions**: The supported intent extensions, in the order the deployment lists them.

extensions.description: The supported intent extensions, in the order the deployment lists them.

items.description: One supported extension, as ``ExtensionSpec.describe()`` lays it out.

scope.description: "intent": keys on the GeoIntent root; "layer": keys on each LayerRef.

summary.description: When to use it, in one line.

required.description: Keys that must be present once the extension is used.

fields_schema.description: JSON schema of the fields (without the prefix).
